claims.claim: Intersect requests $298,250, equivalent to 1,193,000 ADA, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The requested budget is split into WP 1 at 256,000 ADA, WP 2 at 832,000 ADA, and WP 3 at 105,000 ADA.
WP 2 funds the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group to support protocol governance and evolution.

WP 3 will establish a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027, with conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal states that all expenditure will be fully accounted for and any unspent funds returned to the Cardano treasury.
Execution of the work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to the vote, documentation, audited results, and audit report.
The proposal states the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission and links to the relevant governance action.

Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews including deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.

Intersect will use the Sundae Labs treasury management smart contract framework, with published contract addresses, multisig-style authorization thresholds, an external Oversight Committee, and a public dashboard for community auditability.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for a 12-month Intersect TSC support programme with three work packages, external assurance, smart-contract-based fund administration, and several externally checkable references, while also making some accountability and execution claims that remain primarily proposer asserted within the anchor text.
